sentences.text: Stegopelta is a genus of nodosaurid dinosaur belonging to the struthiosaurin group, a family of heavily armored herbivores.
This armored dinosaur measured approximately 4.5 meters in length, stood 1.6 meters high, and weighed around 1000 kilograms.
The original fossil specimen was in poor condition due to erosion and damage from cattle.
Early researchers compared the animal's distinctive armor to that of the giant mammal Glyptodon.
Samuel Wendell Williston described the genus in 1905 based on a partial skeleton found in the Frontier Formation of Fremont County, Wyoming, USA.

Roy Lee Moodie suggested it might be the same as Ankylosaurus in 1910, but Walter Coombs later synonymized it with Nodosaurus until Ken Carpenter and James Kirkland reinstated it in 1998 based on distinct vertebral and armor features.
Stegopelta lived during the middle Cretaceous, approximately 110 to 95 million years ago, with the fossil record spanning from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
It is debated whether Stegopelta is related to the Shamosaurinae subfamily, though the shape of the cervical vertebrae suggests a possible link with Texasetes.
